summary: The strongest direct heavy-ion result is a Bayesian CUJET analysis whose light-hadron-calibrated posterior also describes charm and bottom observables. Other useful contributions address magnetic-field corrections to the QGP equation of state, vorticity contributions to elliptic flow, pion-beam baselines for HADES, symmetry-aware nuclear mass regression, reliability-preserving neural inference, and carefully audited scientific foundation-model transfer.
professional_summary: Bayesian heavy-quark energy loss; magnetic-field QGP thermodynamics; rotating-fireball elliptic flow; HADES pion-beam baselines; symmetry-aware nuclear mass regression; hybrid neural simulation-based inference; audited scientific foundation-model reuse.
strongest_paper: 2609.37729: light-hadron-calibrated Bayesian CUJET predictions for open heavy flavor
strongest_paper_summary: The CUJET study performs the day's strongest cross-sector validation by applying a posterior inferred from light-hadron suppression and anisotropy to charm and bottom observables without heavy-flavor recalibration.

papers.title: Heavy quark energy loss in the Bayesian-inference-improved CUJET model
papers.abstract: CUJET parameters inferred from high-pT light-hadron RAA and v2 also describe charm- and bottom-hadron observables; the derived 2πTDs is broadly consistent with phenomenological and lattice constraints.
papers.summary: A meaningful out-of-sector posterior test supports a common description of high-pT light- and heavy-flavor energy loss, although the physical interpretation remains model conditional.

papers.title: Equation of State of the Quark-Gluon Plasma in an External Magnetic Field to Fourth Order
papers.abstract: A B=0 Taylor method extends the QGP pressure response to O(B4), finding a nonlinear term enhanced near the crossover and visible finite-volume sensitivity.
papers.summary: Relevant nonlinear magnetic response, but coarse Nt=8 ensembles, a roughly two-sigma volume difference, and the calculation's 2014 vintage limit precision use.

papers.title: Elliptic flow in an expanding and rotating fireball
papers.abstract: A rotating thermal fireball changes elliptic flow by an estimated 2-10% across beam energies while leaving midrapidity spectra nearly unchanged.
papers.summary: A useful sensitivity estimate whose magnitude remains strongly dependent on prescribed geometry and rotation rather than dynamical viscous evolution.

papers.title: π-QCD; Proposal for Experiments at the GSI Pion Beam Facility
papers.abstract: HADES proposes pion-nucleon and pion-nucleus measurements of resonances, transition form factors, dileptons, hyperons, and vector mesons up to sqrt(s) about 2.35 GeV.
papers.summary: A credible baseline program for hot-matter interpretation, but a proposal rather than a new heavy-ion measurement.

papers.title: Wigner and mirror correlations in nuclear mass predictions with kernel ridge regression
papers.abstract: Wigner- and mirror-aware kernels reach 98 keV leave-one-out RMS error on known masses, with gains concentrated near N=Z and for mirror pairs.
papers.summary: Substantive physics-informed ML, but extrapolation requires blocked regional tests and calibrated uncertainty beyond leave-one-out validation.

papers.title: Hybrid Neural Simulation-Based Inference for Robust Applications and Limited-Budget Scenarios
papers.abstract: Two hybrid methods approach neural SBI sensitivity at reduced inference cost while retaining some or all parametric reliability guarantees; code is released.
papers.summary: A practical HEP method that treats sensitivity, cost, and guarantees jointly, pending broader simulator-mismatch stress tests.

papers.title: A foundation model for energy and radiation systems built on heterogeneous scientific interfaces
papers.abstract: GEODE couples task-specific interfaces to routed wavelet operators and uses randomized controls to distinguish preserved performance from genuine pretrained reuse across five physical systems.
papers.summary: Unusually rigorous transfer evaluation with a credible detector and simulation-surrogate path, while showing that dedicated operators still win on three of five tasks.

cautions.title: Infrared Subtraction with Artificial Intelligence
cautions.abstract: An AI-assisted local infrared-subtraction construction matches EERAD3 for massless three- and four-jet NLO calculations and sketches NNLO extensions.
cautions.summary: The subtraction idea may be useful, but AI attribution is hard to evaluate scientifically, the benchmark range is narrow, and the NNLO claims remain exploratory.
